dedupe_keys.name: openpra open source probabilistic risk assessment framework and web application

description: OpenPRA is an initiative started by the Probabilistic Risk Assessment Group at North Carolina State University with international partners to build an open platform that integrates probabilistic risk assessment methods and tools, such as event trees, fault trees, Bayesian networks and Markov chains, into one customisable framework. Its stated goals include open source software backed by an international community, hybrid PRA models, ready-to-use models, solvers and transformers, generation of PRA models from model-based systems engineering, web interfaces, examples with guidelines and benchmarks; partners named in 2020 were the University of Stuttgart, TU Dresden and Ufa State Aviation Technical University. The current monorepo holds a React web client, a NestJS REST API, a distributed quantification broker, the SCRAM C++ PRA engine and type definitions for the OpenPSA Model Exchange Format, with deployment guides for local, Docker and Docker Swarm use. It is free under the MIT licence on GitHub, with commits up to 18 September 2026. Coverage is general, with nuclear power plant PRA as the main domain of the group. Caveats: it is research software under active development, deployed as a multi-service web application. Simulation uses are fault and event tree quantification of nuclear plant and supply chain failure risk. Related records: model-cyclus-nuclear-fuel-cycle-simulator is another nuclear engineering tool.
